_meta.what: Dataset-name top-up pass. Raw per-paper output of six extraction agents reading the PDFs in Drive.
_meta.status: ai_draft (unverified) - every name here must be ticked against the printed table before it enters the manuscript
_meta.rule: names are transcribed as printed; programmatically generated groups are recorded as one aggregate with a count, never expanded into invented names

RBBoost / Random Balance.note: 20 + 66 = 86 reconciles. HDDT 'page' is a different binarisation from KEEL 'page-blocks0'; both appear in this one paper.

SplitBal.note: Compact KEEL spelling with no hyphens or underscores. Same 46 sets as RBBoost's KEEL block minus 20, under a different spelling convention: needs canonical mapping before cross-paper counting.

groups.label: Tuning suite (Table 2, 5, held out from evaluation)

CISO.table_ref: Table 1 (37 KEEL + 8 UCI) and Table 2 (5 tuning)
CISO.note: 50 named, not 45: the paper evaluates on 45 and tunes on a disjoint 5. One of the few papers in the corpus with a declared held-out tuning suite - worth flagging as good practice. The extraction renders KEEL '_vs_' as ' vs '; restored to '_vs_' here, so those spellings need a visual check.

groups.label: UCI and KEEL (Table 1, 36; no separate characteristics table)

OBU.table_ref: Table 1 (results table; characteristics are columns of it)
OBU.note: No characteristics table: dataset properties are columns of the results table. Prints 'Segmemt0' (segment0), 'Page-blocks13vs2' (KEEL page-blocks-1-3_vs_4, IR 15.86 matches), 'Shuttle2vs4' (shuttle-c2-vs-c4, IR 20.5 matches). Paper does not say which sets are UCI and which KEEL.

GDO.note: The only paper in this top-up with author-collected (non-public) data: an Internet video traffic set and an esophageal cancer patient set, neither with an identifier-style name and neither shared. Relevant to the reproducibility argument.

FW-SMOTE.note: One of only two papers in the corpus pairing low-dimensional UCI/KEEL sets with high-dimensional microarray sets (n << p). The extraction rendered ' vs ' and en dashes; restored to KEEL '_vs_' and '-' here, so spellings need a visual check.

RBO.note: Declared split between a 10-set preliminary suite and a 24-set final suite. Compact spelling, no separators.

QC-SMOTE.note: Benchmark adopted wholesale from VS-SMOTE, labelled D1-D30 (prefixes stripped here). Paper prints 'newthyroid2' with IR 5.14, but 5.14 is new-thyroid1's IR in every other paper: either the name or the IR is wrong. Left as printed.

aggregates.label: simulated datasets (Experiment I)
aggregates.description: generator grid: imbalance degree N/P in {1.5,3,12,30,60,120} crossed with class overlap 0-100 percent in steps of 10 = 6 x 11 = 66; negatives fixed at 6000, positives varied 50-4000. Never named individually.

NBU.note: 24 + 2 + 66 = 92 reconciles. 72 percent of this paper's headline dataset count is one generator grid. MNIST is used in two scenarios (minority class 3, minority class 5) giving 3 result rows for 2 counted datasets. Shares the Segmemt0 / Page-blocks13vs2 / Abalone09-18 spellings with OBU: same authors, inherited benchmark.

groups.label: KEEL (Table 2 middle, 20 rows printed, text says 19)
generated, listed individually in Table 2 (10 MADELON variations from scikit-learn)

aggregates.label: undersampled copies of the 12 UCI sets
aggregates.description: each UCI set randomly undersampled to raise IR by about x2, x4, x6, x10, x15, x20, kept only where at least 8 minority samples remain. Explicitly omitted from Table 2. The count 48 is the residual 90 - 42, NOT a figure the paper states; upper bound 72.

k-means SMOTE.note: The paper's own table lists 42 rows against a headline of 90. The 48 undersampled copies are inferred as a residual and the paper never states their number, so the headline 90 cannot be reconstructed from the published artifact. Table 2 also truncates KEEL names ('yeast-0-2-5-6' for yeast-0-2-5-6_vs_3-7-8-9), and the 10 'simulated' rows are MADELON variants not labelled as such in the table.

groups.label: base datasets (Table 1 rows without a factor; 27 printed, text says 28)

aggregates.label: undersampled versions (printed in Table 1 as 'NAME (2)' and 'NAME (3)')
aggregates.description: base IR multiplied by 2 and 3 by random undersampling of the minority class, kept where minority count >= 15; 24 rows marked (2) and 18 marked (3).

G-SMOTE.table_ref: Table 1 (all 69 rows printed, sorted by ascending IR)
G-SMOTE.note: 27 + 42 = 69 reconciles with the printed table, but the text says 13 UCI + 13 KEEL + 2 MADELON = 28 base sets, one more than the table prints. Unlike k-means SMOTE this paper does print every variant, so the inflation is visible - but 61 percent of the 69 are re-undersamplings of 27 bases. 'MANDELON' is printed that way (MADELON).

aggregates.label: artificial two-class datasets
aggregates.description: 27 clean sets = 5-dimensional Gaussians, IR in {5,10,25} x size in {500,1000,2500} x majority centre in {[3]^5,[1.7]^5,[1.5]^5}; plus 27 analogous sets with outliers made by swapping 10 percent of each class's instances with the opposite class.

aggregates.label: KEEL real-world datasets
aggregates.description: 15 two-class + 10 multi-class KEEL sets. Real, not generated, but their NAMES appear only in the online supplementary document, not in the PDF. Table 3 reports average ranks only.

DLexiBoost.table_ref: Table 3 (ranks only), Table 4; no table lists dataset names
DLexiBoost.note: 8 + 54 + 25 = 87. The paper never states 87 itself. No table in the PDF names a single dataset: 54 are generated and unnamed, 25 are real but named only in supplementary material, 8 are named in running text. The headline count cannot be checked from the PDF alone. GAP REMAINS: the 25 KEEL names need the supplementary file.

CGMOS.note: Names are the paper's own abbreviations, not repository identifiers: 'Statlog', 'Customers', 'PlanRelax' do not say which UCI set is meant, and Statlog alone covers at least six different UCI datasets. Table 3 spells UKnowledge as 'UserKnowledge'. Reproducing this benchmark requires guessing.

SVDD-WSMOTE.note: Table 2's 24 rows are only 15 distinct base sets: Yeast appears 9 times and Pageblock twice under different class combinations, i.e. 9 of the 24 'datasets' are re-splits of yeast. Text says 16 base sets but the table shows 15. Printed Table 8 shows 7 of the 8 bearing combinations (NC appears only in the text). Simulated sets are named only A-D.

aggregates.label: motivation-only synthetic radial scenarios (Fig. 2 / Table 1)
aggregates.description: two-class radial sets at 50:1000 skew on a 3x3 grid of positive density (High/Medium/Low) x centroid separation (High/Medium/Low); referred to by (density, separation) pair labels, not by names; not part of the 20-set evaluation.

LS.note: Clean separation between a 9-scenario synthetic motivation study and a 20-set real evaluation, and the headline count covers only the latter. Spelling drifts between tables ('Breast-W' vs 'Breast-w', 'SVMGuide1' vs 'SVMguide1'). Compustat and Intrusion carry fixed train/test splits.

Global-CS (AAAI).note: Synthetic sets are named individually (2 attributes, 3 or 5 classes, random normal distributions), so they are listed rather than aggregated. First 10 rows balanced, last 10 imbalanced - a deliberate design, not an accident.

Global-CS (journal).note: VERIFIED IDENTICAL to the AAAI version: same 20 names, same order, same sizes, attributes, classes and class distributions. The journal extension reuses the conference benchmark unchanged.

INOS.title: Integrated Oversampling for Imbalanced Time Series Classification

groups.label: UCR time series, main evaluation (names from running text; Table 1 body is an image)
additional UCR sets (named in text; results only on the authors' website)

aggregates.label: imbalanced two-class apportions
aggregates.description: built from the 7 balanced UCR sets by taking one class positive and the rest negative (Adiac 37 classes, FaceAll 14, 50words 50, SLeaf 15); the apportion list is only in the image of Table 1. These are re-splits of the 7 counted UCR sets, not additional datasets.

INOS.metrics: F-Value; G-Mean; Precision; Recall; True Negative Rate
INOS.note: NEW PAPER. Second case in the corpus of an unreadable image table (with MWMOTE). Every source dataset is originally BALANCED and binarised by the authors - a pure Modified-data paper. Claims 'significantly better' with no named statistical test. 7 further UCR sets are named but their results live only on a website.

SMOTE-IPF.title: SMOTE-IPF: Addressing the noisy and borderline examples problem in imbalanced classification by a re-sampling method with filtering

aggregates.label: synthetic with borderline examples (Table 3)
aggregates.description: 3 shapes (sub-cluster, clover, paw) x IR in {5,7} x disturbance ratio in {0,30,50,60,70} percent; 600 examples at IR 5, 800 at IR 7. Named by their parameter triple, not by dataset names.

aggregates.label: noise-injected copies of the 9 real-world sets
aggregates.description: 9 datasets x noise level in {20,40} percent x noise type in {class, attribute}.

SMOTE-IPF.classifiers: C4.5 (main); k-NN, SVM, RIPPER, PART (web page only)
SMOTE-IPF.note: NEW PAPER. 9 real datasets out of a headline 75: 88 percent of the benchmark is synthetic or author-perturbed. Reports per-dataset results for all of it and runs a proper statistical protocol, so the inflation is transparent rather than hidden. Results for 4 of the 5 classifiers are off-paper.

HDE.title: A hybrid data-level ensemble to enable learning from highly imbalanced dataset

groups.label: LibSVM, minority instances randomly removed by the authors to raise IR (Table 1, 14)

HDE.classifiers: C4.5 base (40 per ensemble); vs SMOTEBoost, EUSBoost, RUSBoost, SMOTEBagging, UnderBagging, EasyEnsemble, IIVotes, CBIS, SNGEIP, sNED
HDE.note: NEW PAPER. Declares its own modification in the table: 14 of 42 sets are LibSVM data the authors undersampled to manufacture high IR, and the Source column says so. Datasets uploaded to GitHub. IR 9.08 to 970.6. A clean example of modified data that is labelled as modified.

NROMM.title: Noise-robust oversampling for imbalanced data classification

aggregates.label: binary datasets D1-D10 (Table 6)
aggregates.description: ten binary sets labelled D1 to D10 for the SVM comparison; their identities are given only in the supplementary material, not in the paper.

NROMM.metrics: AvAcc; MG; CBA; CEN (multi-class); AUC; G-mean (binary)
NROMM.table_ref: Table 2; Table 3 (7 of 20 datasets); Table 4; Table 6
NROMM.note: NEW PAPER. Table 3 prints C5.0 results for only 7 of the 20 datasets; the full per-dataset results for all 20 datasets x 4 classifiers are in supplementary material, and the 10 binary sets are anonymous D1-D10 in the paper. Directly relevant to the reporting-granularity axis. Baselines include MC-CCR, MC-RBO, MDO, SMOM, SMOTE-IPF, KNNOR.

GOIO.title: GOIO: Generative Oversampling Approach to Class Imbalance and Overlap of Tabular Data

groups.label: artificial, authors' own Gaussian generator (Table II, 5)

GOIO.table_ref: Table I, Table II; per-dataset results in Tables V-VII
GOIO.note: NEW PAPER. Tables I and II are images; names transcribed from the rendered page. Baselines: SMOTE, SMOTETL, MLOS, BSMOTE, GAMO, SOS, plus an IDENTITY control. CTGAN and cWGAN were EXCLUDED on the authors' own preliminary judgement of 'lower synthesis quality'; TVAE and TabDDPM not compared. GOIO itself builds on Tabsyn. Prints 'taiwanses'. All 18 real sets public, none author-collected.

DGOT.title: Diffusion GAN-Based Oversampling for Imbalanced Tabular Data
DGOT.classifiers: XGBoost; KNN; DTC; Logistic Regression; RFC
DGOT.table_ref: Table I; per-dataset results in Tables IV-VI
DGOT.note: NEW PAPER. Table I is an image; names transcribed from the rendered page. 15 binary + 7 multi-class. Compares CTGAN, TVAE and SOS alongside SMOTE, BSMOTE, SMOTETL and an IDENTITY control: the most complete generative baseline set in the corpus. Same group as GOIO, and the benchmarks overlap heavily (default, abalone_15, abalone_6, optical_digits, sick_euthyroid, thyroid_sick, wine_quality) though the lists are not identical.

Loyalty-SMOTE.title: Loyalty-SMOTE: Data synthesis algorithm for effective imbalanced data classification

groups.label: group 1, UCI/KEEL (Table 2; text says 30, table prints 31)
group 3, Kaggle (Table 4; text claims 9, table prints 8)
group 3, name appearing only in runtime Table 14

Loyalty-SMOTE.note: NEW PAPER. 60 entries printed, 59 distinct ('Bankruptcy' appears in both group 1 and group 5 with the same 6820 instances and IR 31). Group counts do not reconcile: group 1 claims 30 but prints 31; group 3 claims 9, Table 4 prints 8 omitting bank-full while Table 14 prints bank-full and omits parkinson. Spelling drifts between description and result tables (wdbc/WDBC, bezediris/bezdeiris, darwin/Darwin). One classifier only, no statistical test, best-count comparison only - the weakest evaluation protocol among the 2026 papers.
